_doc.overview: The art kit of the town (tools/make_town_art.py draws it; assets/town holds the pictures). Everything is seen from above, lit from the top left (soft shadows fall to the south east), dark brown outline (#221a13), muted colours: the look of the yard's own art. `items` lists every piece; each has an id, a category, a footprint in tiles and its sprites. Tiles: the pictures are drawn at `tile_px` = 128 px to the tile (the game's TILE is 64 px, so draw a picture at 64 / 128 = 0.5 scale); the ground and the floors are 4 x 4 atlases of `ground_piece_px` = 64 px pieces (one piece to the tile, 64 px: draw them at scale 1; the tile at (x, y) shows piece (x % 4, y % 4), as assets/terrain does, but with 64 px pieces instead of 128: world.gd `_build_ground` must use texture width / 4 for its piece size).

item.category: street | house | roof | floor | furniture | outdoors | fortify | marker
item.kind: ground_atlas (a ground or floor: grid [4, 4] of piece_px pieces) | atlas (a grid of cells in one picture: `cells` maps a name to [col, row], `cell_px` is the cell's size; an autotile set keys its cells by neighbour mask) | wall_fill / roof_fill (seamless 128 px tiles, with `edges` naming their autotile overlay) | prop (one or more pictures of one thing, packed in one PNG; see `sprites`) | overlay
item.layer: ground (the terrain: under everything) | decal (flat things on the ground or floor: paint, rugs, stains, steps; under the people) | object (things that stand: furniture, trees, cars; depth-sorted with the people on the footprint's bottom edge, or `sort_y`) | wall (wall cells and what is set into them: doors, windows, barricades) | roof (hidden when the avatar is inside)
item.footprint: [w, h] in tiles for the default facing (s). The cells the thing covers; w and h swap for facing e and w (each sprite has its own `fp`).
item.anchor: [ax, ay] in tiles: where the footprint's top left corner lies inside the picture (the picture has a soft shadow and sometimes a roof or crown outside the footprint). To put a thing on cell (cx, cy): its picture's top left goes to (cx - ax, cy - ay) tiles. Same for every facing.
item.sort_y: (optional) tiles from the picture's top to the line the thing is depth-sorted on (default: anchor y + footprint h)
item.solid: "all" (every footprint cell blocks walking and the dead) | [] (walkable) | [[x, y], ...] (cells that block) | {state: bool} (by state, e.g. a door: closed true, open false)
item.tags: container (can be searched: it has a `closed` and an `opened` state) | solid | walkable | door | window | opening | roof | hideable | wall | autotile | fence | gate | fortify | marker | decal | clutter | base (the base's radio and stash) | reused (made from the yard's existing pictures) | ...
item.states: (optional) e.g. [closed, opened] (a container: opened = searched), [closed, open, broken] (a door), [intact, broken, boarded] (a window)
item.facings: (optional) [s, w, n, e]: the way the front faces. s: the back is to the north wall, the front to the south; turn clockwise for w, n, e. A door's facing is the side the OUTSIDE is on. `orients` [h, v] instead: along x or along y.
item.variants: (optional) how many looks (a colour, a book shelf's books). Every variant has the same states and facings. `variant_names` names them where it matters ([built, damaged] for the fortification pieces).
item.sprites: [{file, rect: [x, y, w, h] (pixels inside the PNG), facing | orient, state, variant, slope, fp: [w, h] (footprint of this sprite)}...]: pick the sprite whose fields match what you want and draw its rect. A key an item has no use for is absent.
item.note: what it is, and anything particular to place it right

_doc.autotiles: Walls, roofs, fences, hedges, sandbags, the kerb and the wall shadows come as `atlas` items whose cells are chosen by a 4 bit mask of the neighbours (N 1, E 2, S 4, W 8; col = mask % 4, row = mask // 4). Walls and roof edges use the mask of the OPEN sides (the neighbour is not a wall / not roof); fences, hedges and sandbags use the mask of the CONNECTED sides (the neighbour is the same kind of line).

recipes.wall: for each wall cell draw wall_<material> (variant a, b for one cell in six) then wall_edges cell [mask of open sides] over it. A door cell is not a wall for the mask; a window cell is. On every non wall cell next to a wall draw wall_shadows (n: wall to the north, w: to the west, nw: both, diag_nw: only the corner). Doors replace the wall cell; windows and barricades are laid over it.
recipes.roof: give a rectangle of roof cells: the ridge runs along the longer side; the half to the north (or west) uses the `lit` fill, the other the `shade` fill (turn the pictures a quarter turn counter clockwise for a ridge along y); lay the ridge strip along the middle line; lay roof_edge_<material> cell [mask of open sides] over every cell (it overhangs 0.2 tile and throws its shadow). Hide all roof layer pieces while the avatar is inside that building.
recipes.street: asphalt cells (three variants in blocks), lane_markings cells over them, sidewalk cells with kerb cells over them where road touches, lawn / dirt_path / gravel for yards and drives, leaves / manhole / drain as decals; lawn_edge on the lawn cells that touch paving or a wall and lawn_patch here and there on the lawn (soft transitions and no seen repeat); streetlamp and hydrant on the sidewalks. scripts/town/town_world.gd and town_chunk_paint.gd draw all of this.
recipes.container: a container has states closed / opened: draw closed until searched, then opened; the `marker_searched` tick can float over it.

light: top left (shadows fall to the south east)

items.note: Road surface: a 4 x 4 atlas of 64 px pieces, seamless when repeated (tile (x, y) shows piece (x % 4, y % 4), as assets/terrain does). a: worn with hairline cracks and oil stains; b: cracked, one pothole; c: two repair patches. All three share the same grain, so they can border each other: mix them in blocks.
Sidewalk slabs, one slab to the tile, grass in the joints; a 4 x 4 atlas of 64 px pieces. Three variants (a: tidy, b: cracked, c: overgrown).
Lawn; a 4 x 4 atlas of 64 px pieces. a: plain, b: clover and daisies, c: worn patches and long clumps. Same base, so they mix.
Packed dirt for paths and back yards; a 4 x 4 atlas of 64 px pieces. a: dry with stones, b: damp and trodden.
Gravel for driveways; a 4 x 4 atlas of 64 px pieces. a: grey, b: tan with weeds.

Road paint, laid over asphalt cells (worn, so it is see-through in places). dash_*: a dash half a cell long, the next cell continues the pattern; double_*: a yellow double centre line; edge_n/e/s/w: a white edge line near the named side of the cell (the side that is next to the kerb); cross_h / cross_v: one bar of a zebra crossing (h: the bar runs along x, for a crossing over a road that runs east to west: stack cells along y); stop_h / stop_v: a stop line (h: across a road that runs north to south).

The kerb, laid on a SIDEWALK cell. s/w/n/e: a stone along the named edge (the side the road is on); corner_se..: the sidewalk's own corner is rounded (the roads are on both named sides: asphalt fills the corner); inner_se..: the sidewalk cell's neighbours on the two named sides are sidewalk but the cell diagonally there is road (a street corner seen from its other side): a quarter disc of road bites into the cell. A cell is 160 x 160 px = 1.25 tiles, anchor (0, 0): the extra quarter to the right and below holds the stone's soft shadow, so the picture is laid with its top left on the cell's top left.
Fallen leaves, scattered, laid over any ground cell (sidewalk, lawn, asphalt). Rotate or flip at will.
A cast iron manhole cover on a road or sidewalk cell. Flush with the ground: walkable, no shadow.

A storm drain grate along a kerb (h: along x; the picture is 1 x 0.5 tiles and sits at the cell's top for h, left for v after the turn: place its picture on the road cell next to the kerb). Flush with the ground.

The edge of a LAWN cell where a side of it meets paving, road, wall or a fence (bare soil, a ragged line, blades): n/e/s/w name the side that touches; a corner cell takes two. Laid on the lawn cell itself (128 px = the tile), over the lawn, under everything that stands.

A soft patch of different grass (dry, lush, bare earth, fresh), 1.5 x 1.5 tiles, centred where you lay it, over a lawn here and there to break up the repeat of the lawn atlas (the three lawns are laid in blocks of 4 x 4).
A fire hydrant on a sidewalk (a: red, b: yellow). Walkable around it; it is only a picture that blocks nothing.

A street lamp seen from above: the foot in the cell, the arm leaning out over the street and the lamp head at its end. Facing = the way the arm points (s: toward the south, so the post stands on the north sidewalk of an east-west street).

The outline and the rims of a wall top, laid over a wall fill (wall_<material>) on a wall cell. Cell index = mask of the OPEN sides (the neighbour on that side is not a wall): N 1 + E 2 + S 4 + W 8; col = index % 4, row = index // 4. A door cell is NOT a wall for this (the wall ends in front of it get their outline); a window cell IS a wall (the wall runs on through it).

Soft wall shadows, laid on floor or ground cells (not on the wall itself). n: the cell's north neighbour is a wall; w: its west neighbour is a wall; nw: both; diag_nw: neither, but the cell to the north west is (a small dab in the corner). Light comes from the top left.

A front door in a wall cell (replaces the wall cell: a full 128 px picture with its doorway floor, its frame and its leaf: opaque, so the open picture can be faded in over the shut one). facing = the side the OUTSIDE is on (s: the wall runs along x with the street to the south; e: the wall runs along y with the street to the east). 12 variants: 6 door colours (0-1 oxblood with three lights, 2-3 blue grey, 4-5 dark green with panels, 6-7 sage green ledged boards on strap hinges, 8-9 natural wood, 10-11 walnut) x the side of the hinge (even variants hinged on the left of the picture as seen from outside, odd on the right). The game gives the two cells of a doorway the variants n and n + 1: one colour hinged at the outer jambs when n is even; when n is odd the pair is the right hand leaf of one colour and the left hand leaf of the next in the ring of colours, mostly a near neighbour (green and sage, wood and walnut, walnut and oxblood, blue grey and green; oxblood and blue grey, sage and wood are the odd pairs). Open: the leaf swung inward about 60 degrees with its swing drawn on the floor; broken: the leaf hangs splintered, a piece on the sill, the frame torn. The look is the same in every state, so a door keeps its colour when it is opened or broken. A closed door blocks; open and broken do not. Not a wall for wall_edges (the wall ends beside it get their outline). Every facing is lit from the north west like the rest.

An inside door in a partition wall cell, same rules as door_front: a thinner, lighter leaf in a plain frame, on a threshold board. facing: s for a partition that runs along x, e for one that runs along y (the only two the game asks for: a door in a partition has no outside, so there is no n or w). 16 variants: 4 leaves in runs of four (0-3 white, 4-7 cream, 8-11 light oak, 12-15 powder blue) x the side of the hinge (even: left, odd: right). A doorway with no door needs no picture: leave a floor cell in the wall.
An overhead garage door, 3 cells wide (the wall run it replaces), facing the way the outside is (s: the wall runs along x). Picture 3 x 1 tiles for s and n, 1 x 3 for e and w.

A window set into a wall top: laid OVER a wall cell (the wall fill and its edges stay underneath), h for a wall that runs along x, v for one that runs along y. The cell stays a wall (solid, and a wall for wall_edges) in every state; the sim decides who can see or climb through. Variants: a plain white frame, b wooden frame with curtains (curtains only while intact).

The step in front of a door: 3 cells wide, 1 deep, laid on the ground cells outside the door, centred on it (a: concrete, b: wooden planks). Facing = the side it faces, away from the house (s: it lies south of a door in a wall that runs along x). Walkable.

A porch deck 3 x 2 cells in front of a door with a rail round its sides and the front, open in the middle for the steps. Facing = the side it faces, away from the house. Walkable. White rail. Its roof, if any, is a roof piece.

items.name: Terracotta tiles
items.note: Terracotta tiles: seamless 128 px roof tiles. For a gable roof with its ridge along x the north slope uses `lit` and the south slope `shade`; for a ridge along y turn the pictures a quarter turn counter clockwise (west lit, east shade). Variant b has a decal (moss, missing tiles): use it for about one cell in eight. `ridge` is a cap strip (1 x 1 cell, the strip in the middle third) laid along the ridge line; for an even number of rows the ridge falls on the line between two rows: lay it half a tile off. `edges` is the eave overlay set to lay on the border cells.

The eave of a terracotta tiles roof, laid on a roof cell over its fill: cell index = mask of the OPEN sides (the neighbour is not roof): N 1 + E 2 + S 4 + W 8; col = index % 4, row = index // 4. A cell is 224 px = 1.75 tiles with the roof cell at (0.25, 0.25) tiles, so lay the cell's picture with its top left 0.25 tile up and left of the roof cell. The roof reaches 0.2 tile past the cell on every open side (over the wall below), with fascia, outline and a soft shadow to the south and east.

The same with the runner along y.

Bathroom tile, small tiles (a quarter cell) with dirty grout, cracks and damp stains: 4 x 4 atlas of 64 px pieces; a: pale blue, b: off white.
A fridge, back to the north (facing s: its door faces south). States: closed / opened (searched: the door stands ajar). Variants: white, cream.
A kitchen counter cell with cupboard doors in front. Opened: a door stands ajar. Variants: a chopping board, a pot and a plate.
A counter with a steel sink and a draining board.
A cooker with four rings. Variants: white, black.
A tall cupboard or pantry. Opened: its doors stand ajar. Variants: wood, painted white.

An armchair, back to the north.

A low table with magazines and a mug.
A dining table, two cells wide (a: bare wood with a bowl, b: a white cloth and two plates). Put a `chair` on the cells along its long sides.
A chair; facing is the way the seat looks (s: back at the north). a: wooden dining chair, b: office swivel chair. Not solid: the dead and the people can walk over it.
A bookcase two cells wide, books to the front. Opened: gaps in the rows and a book on the floor. The two variants have different books.
A desk with three drawers in front (a: papers, a pen and a lamp; b: a ledger, a mug and a tin). Opened: a drawer stands out.
A toilet, cistern to the north. a: lid down, b: seat up.
A bathtub two cells long, taps at its west end (facing s). b: a dirty one.
A washbasin (a: pedestal, b: on a vanity cupboard).
A small wall cabinet with a red cross, fixed to the north of its cell (so it takes no floor room: not solid). Opened: the mirror door swings out.
A red steel toolbox on the floor. Opened: the lid is up, tools show.
A workbench with a vise and tools, drawers in front. Opened: a drawer stands out.
A cardboard box (three sizes). Opened: the flaps are up and the inside shows.
A wooden crate. Opened: a slat is prised off and the inside shows.
A wicker laundry basket of clothes. Opened: clothes pulled out and dropped at its edge. Round: no facings.
A steel shelf with rows of tins, seen from above. Opened: tins missing, one rolled off.
A worn rug, 3 x 2 cells (facing s or n: the same picture; turn it for 2 x 3 with e or w if you add them). It lies on the floor under the furniture.
A round rug, 2 x 2 cells (a: sage and cream, b: blue and cream).
A standing lamp seen from above, a round shade (a: cream, b: red). A light source can sit on it.
THE BASE'S RADIO: a field radio set with a morse key, a notepad, headphones and a coil of aerial wire on a table, two cells wide. The set faces south.
THE BASE'S STASH: a chest with iron straps and a lock. Opened: the lid is thrown back, cloth and a tin inside.
Scattered papers on the floor (a third has a coffee ring). Rotate or flip freely.
Shards of broken glass. Rotate or flip freely.
A blood stain (b and c have a drag mark). Rotate or flip freely.
A dropped bag (a: a backpack, b: a paper bag spilled with a tin rolled out). Rotate freely.
A loose mattress on the floor, one cell by two (a: striped ticking, b: stained and torn).

A white picket fence (a post in each cell, a rail with pickets in front of it). items.note: A wooden fence of heavy planks on thick posts, the first fence the community builds: strong enough for a night or two. DAMAGED: boards torn out, splintered, weathered. Cell index = mask of the CONNECTED sides (the neighbour on that side is the same kind of line): N 1 + E 2 + S 4 + W 8; col = index % 4, row = index // 4; index 0 is a lone post. The line runs through the middle of the cell. Cells are 128 x 128 px, anchor (0, 0), footprint 1 x 1.
items.name: Wooden palisade fence (damaged)

items.note: A reinforced fence: planks and corrugated steel sheet on steel posts. Holds longer than the wooden fence. DAMAGED: dented, rusted, torn open. Cell index = mask of the CONNECTED sides (the neighbour on that side is the same kind of line): N 1 + E 2 + S 4 + W 8; col = index % 4, row = index // 4; index 0 is a lone post. The line runs through the middle of the cell. Cells are 128 x 128 px, anchor (0, 0), footprint 1 x 1.
items.name: Reinforced fence (damaged)

items.note: A wall of sandbags, two courses of bags. DAMAGED: bags burst, sand spilled. Cell index = mask of the CONNECTED sides (the neighbour on that side is the same kind of line): N 1 + E 2 + S 4 + W 8; col = index % 4, row = index // 4; index 0 is a lone post. The line runs through the middle of the cell. Cells are 128 x 128 px, anchor (0, 0), footprint 1 x 1.
items.name: Sandbags (damaged)

items.note: The fence gate of the perimeter, two cells wide (replaces two cells of the fence line), between two thick posts: closed, or open (both leaves swung back). variant 0 is the BUILT look, variant 1 the DAMAGED one (a board torn out, hanging). h: in a fence that runs along x with the outside to the south; v: in one that runs along y. A closed gate blocks.

A corner watchtower: a 2 x 2 deck on stilts with a plank and sandbag parapet, a searchlight and a ladder. The picture is 2.5 tiles tall because the stilts show below the deck: the footprint is the bottom 2 rows (anchor y 0.5 + padding). variant 0 BUILT, variant 1 DAMAGED (a hole in the deck, a plank gone).

A floodlight on a pole with four lamps, a block and sandbags at its foot: 1.4 x 3.4 tiles, the footprint is the block's cell at the bottom (anchor (0.2, 3.0) + padding). variant 0 BUILT (lamps lit: put the engine's light on the head), variant 1 DAMAGED (leaning, two lamps smashed, a cable hanging).

The same gate three cells wide (the base's gate slot is three tiles): closed, or open (both leaves swung back); variant 0 BUILT, 1 DAMAGED; h: in a fence that runs along x with the outside to the south; v: along y. A closed gate blocks.

A lookout post for one shooter on a 1 x 2 tile footprint (the tower's slot tile and the post tile beside it): a deck on stilts with a plank and sandbag parapet, a searchlight and a ladder. The picture is 2.34 tiles tall because the stilts show below the deck: the footprint is the bottom 2 rows (anchor y 0.34 + padding). variant 0 BUILT, variant 1 DAMAGED (a hole in the deck, a plank gone). The shooter stands on the deck: draw it under the people.

What is left where a fence section has fallen: planks and splinters on the ground and the stump of a post, walkable. Cells are 128 x 128 px, anchor (0, 0), footprint 1 x 1; the top row lies along x (a fence that runs east to west), the bottom row along y; four looks each (pick one by the tile's coordinates). Draw it on every tile of a section that is down.
items.name: Fallen fence

items.note: Two planks crossed in an X with a steel strap, laid OVER `barricade_door`: the barred door that has the plank kit. variant 0 BUILT, 1 DAMAGED (one plank snapped).
Heavy planks and a brace over a window cell: lay it OVER the wall cell and the window (h: a wall that runs along x). variant 0 BUILT, variant 1 DAMAGED (a plank broken, the brace snapped).
A door cell barricaded with planks and a heavy bar: lay it OVER the door cell (h: the wall runs along x). variant 0 BUILT, variant 1 DAMAGED.

An 'enter' doorway chevron for a door cell or the cell in front of it: two chevrons pointing the way you go (facing s: they point south, so for a front door in a south wall you want n, pointing into the house). Pulse its alpha in the engine.
A tick on a dark badge, half a tile across (64 px), for a container that has been searched: float it over the container's middle.
